titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§165–168: Senggum's Pride, Jamuqa's Plot, and the Feast That Was Not Eaten
part: §§165–168 — Senggum's Pride, Jamuqa's Plot, and the Feast That Was Not Eaten
about: Four sections. §165: Chinggis Qahan, wishing a closer tie, asks for Senggum's sister Cha'ur-Beki for Jüchi and offers a bride in exchange; Senggum, proud, refuses and complains of rank, and Chinggis's heart cools towards Wang Qan and his son. §166: in the spring of the Pig year Jamuqa and a company of others meet Senggum, slander Temüjin as one with words and envoys to the Naiman, and propose to seize him. §167: Senggum sends the slander to his father; Wang Qan at first defends Temüjin, then gives way. §168: Senggum plans a betrothal feast as a trap; Father Münlig, with whom Chinggis lodges on the way, warns him, and he sends two men in his place, who are noticed. The Ming glosses carry most of the weight, and several clauses are marked in the notes as first readings or not understood.

sentences.t: Amaraγ deġere dabqur amaraγ boluja keġen Čiṅgis Qaγan sedkižü
sentences.l: Close, above, double, close, let-us-become, saying, Čiṅgis Qaγan thinking,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, thinking "Let us be close, and over and above that doubly close,"
sentences.n: Read this as a quotation closed by keġen 'saying' (the stock closer, which comes back again and again) followed by the thinker and his converb: 'Amaraγ … boluja' keġen … sedkižü, 'saying "…", thinking'. The converb -žü/-žu (Ming 着, 'doing it and …') is the chain-link of the whole text; -žü after a front vowel, -žu after a back vowel (vowel harmony), so sedkižü, but later baižu. amaraγ is 'close, intimate' (Ming 親厚); deġere ('above, on top' elsewhere) is glossed 一面 here, 'one side, besides', and dabqur 'layered, doubled' (重). I read them together as 'close, and over and above that doubly close'; the weight of deġere here is uncertain. boluja is bol- 'become' + hortative -uja (the u a linking vowel, as in abuja), the Ming's 咱 marking 'let us' (inclusive). That this means a marriage tie laid on top of the pact of §164 is my inference from what follows; the Ming does not say so.

morph.gloss: hortative: let us … (the u a linking vowel, as in abuja)
Chinggis, the title of Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Žüči-de Seṅgüm-ün döġi Čaγ̇ur-Beki-ji γuirun Seṅgüm-ün köġün Tasaqa-da bidan-u Qožin-Beki-ji aralžin ögüje keġen γuiγ̇asu
sentences.l: Žüči-to, Seṅgüm-of younger-sister Čaγ̇ur-Beki-(object), asking-when, Seṅgüm-of son Tasaqa-to, our Qožin-Beki-(object), exchanging, let-us-give, saying, if-asking,
sentences.i: When he asked for Senggum's younger sister Cha'ur-Beki for Jüchi, and, saying "Let us give our Qojin-Beki to Senggum's son Tasaqa in exchange," made the request,
sentences.n: A long, slow clause, so I cut it at its conditional. The names come with their case endings: Žüči-de (Ming 行, dative-locative 'to, for'), the two -ji (accusative; the Ming marks it 行, which is how it renders an object marker), Tasaqa-da. Seṅgüm-ün … döġi is 'Senggum's younger sister' with the possessor before the noun, as always. The bride-exchange is aralžin ögüje, 'exchanging, let us give' (Ming 相換 與咱); aralžin is read as one word, its stem aral- is a guess from the Ming. The quotation 'Seṅgüm-ün köġün … ögüje' is closed by keġen. Then γuiγ̇asu, conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 呵, 'if/when'), and the speaker is not named; I take it to be Chinggis, carried over from the previous unit. The Ming's 索 'ask for' is the only handle on the stems γui-/γuju-/γuγ̇-, which I treat as one verb in different spellings; this is uncertain. Who is 'our' Qožin-Beki: the Ming says 女名, 'a woman's name', only; I take her to be of Chinggis's household.

Senggum, son of Wang Qan (personal name) [人名的]
Cha'ur-Beki, a woman's name (beki, a title of rank, uncertain) [妹名 行]

sentences.t: tende Seṅgüm öġer(i)-jen jekežilen sedkižü ügülerün:
sentences.l: There, Seṅgüm, own-self great-making, thinking, saying:
sentences.i: Then Senggum, thinking himself a great man, said:
sentences.n: tende 'there, then' (Ming 那裏) is a plain turn of the story. öġer(i)-jen is 'one's own', the reflexive-possessive -(i)jen added to öġer 'self' (Ming 自己 自的行): a pattern to watch for, because it always points back to the subject, here Senggum. jekežilen is jeke 'great' + -žile- 'to act as' + converb -n, Ming 大做, 'making [himself] great': I read it as 'puffing himself up, acting the grandee'. sedkižü and ügülerün are the converbs of thinking and speaking; -rün, 'when/while saying' (Ming 說), is the usual way into a speech, closed here by the colon Shiratori prints.

morph.gloss: Senggum, son of Wang Qan (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: "Bidan-u uruγ an-dur oduγ̇asu alaγ̇u- n-a baižu eġenegče qoimar qaraqu ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: "Our kin them-to if-go, door-rear-at standing, intently the-front looking, were.
sentences.i: "When our kinsmen go to them, they stand at the back by the door, looking intently toward the front.
sentences.n: Senggum's complaint about rank at the visits between the two houses. bidan-u uruγ is 'our kin' (uruγ, Ming 親, 'kin, offspring'), an-dur 'to them' (Ming 他每行; an- is the third-person stem, the back-vowel partner of in-). oduγ̇asu is od- 'go' + conditional -uγ̇asu (Ming 去呵), 'if/when one goes'; the -γ̇asu ending (back-vowel) and -ġesü (front-vowel) are the conditionals to look for. alaγ̇u- + n-a is one word split at the line end, alaγ̇un-a 'at the rear of the door', Ming 門後行; the -n- is a linking n and -a the dative-locative (行). qoimar is 'the front' (Ming 正面), eġenegče 'intently' (專一, form uncertain). The word-for-word sense, 'our kin standing at the door-rear looking to the front', reads as the lowly place of guests; the next unit makes the contrast. ažuγ̇u is a- 'be' + past -žuγ̇u, 'was'. ažuγ̇u after the participle qaraqu makes a past habitual; `l` keeps 'were', but `i` uses the present, 'they stand', which suits a complaint.

morph.gloss: the rear of the door (first half of a split word) [門後]
the front, the front part [正面]

sentences.t: An-u uruγ bidan-dur ireġesü qoimar-a saγ̇užu alaγ̇un-a qaran ažuγ̇u"
sentences.l: Their kin us-to if-come, front-at sitting, door-rear-at looking, were".
sentences.i: When their kinsmen come to us, they sit at the front, looking toward the back by the door."
sentences.n: The mirror of the previous unit: An-u uruγ 'their kin' (the genitive -u after back vowels, the back-vowel companion of in-ü, but here standing before its noun) and bidan-dur 'to us'. ireġesü is ire- 'come' + front-vowel conditional -ġesü (Ming 來呵), saγ̇užu 'sitting' (坐着), qoimar-a 'at the front' (正面(行)). The Ming gives qaran only in brackets (看), which I take as the glossator's sign that he is inferring the sense; the form is qara- + converb -n. (The Ming writes 俺 'we, exclusive' for bidan-dur although the form is the inclusive bida-; the glossators are going by sense.) I read 'they sit at the front looking toward the door-rear', that is, looking down on us; my own reading of the picture, not one the Ming states. The closing quotation mark sits on ažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: the front, the front part [正面(行)]
the rear of the door [門後行]

sentences.t: keġen öġer(i)-jen jekežilen sedkižü bidan-i doramžilan ügüležü Čaγ̇ur-Beki-ji ülü ögün ese taγ̇alažuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: Saying, own-self great-making, thinking, us looking-down-on, speaking, Čaγ̇ur-Beki-(object) not giving, not-yet pleased-was.
sentences.i: So, thinking himself great and slighting us in his speech, he would not give Cha'ur-Beki, and was not pleased.
sentences.n: The speech is shut by keġen and the chain of converbs resumes: keġen, jekežilen, sedkižü, doramžilan, ügüležü, each Ming 着 or its like, all with Senggum as subject. doramžilan is doramžila- 'look down on' (Ming 下覷着) + -n; ügüležü with its front-vowel -žü, against baižu with back-vowel -žu earlier, shows the harmony again. ülü ögün is 'not giving' (ülü, Ming 不, with a converb: the negative for present or converb forms), and then ese taγ̇alažuγ̇ui, ese + past, Ming 不曾 喜有, 'did not [yet] take pleasure'. That is the pair to keep in mind: ülü with converbs and non-past forms, ese with the past. The sense of taγ̇alažuγ̇ui is shaky: the Ming 喜 is 'be pleased', which in the next sections turns into 愛 'love'; here I take it as 'was not pleased [with the match]', although 'did not consent' is possible.

morph.gloss: to look down on, slight [下覷着]
Cha'ur-Beki, a woman's name [女名 行]
not (negates a present or future action, or a converb) [不]
to be pleased, to like [喜有]

sentences.t: Tere üge-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan dotora-γ̇an Waṅ-Qān Nilqa-Seṅgüm qojar-tur dura qočorčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: That word-in, Čiṅgis Qaγan, inside-own, Waṅ-Qān, Nilqa-Seṅgüm, the-two-to, heart was-left-behind.
sentences.i: Because of those words, Chinggis Qahan's heart cooled, within himself, towards the two, Wang Qan and Nilqa-Senggum.
sentences.n: tere üge-dür is 'in that speech' (Ming 言語 裏), 'because of that'. dotora-γ̇an, 'in one's own inside' (Ming 心 內), takes the reflexive-possessive -γ̇an after a vowel and points to the subject, Chinggis. qojar-tur: qojar 'two' follows the pair it counts (Waṅ-Qān, Nilqa-Seṅgüm) and takes the dative-locative -tur, Ming 兩箇行. dura qočorčuγ̇u is 'heart was left behind' (Ming 心 落後了有來), a figure for 'his feeling for them fell away' (the Ming's 落後 is 'left behind'; 'cooled' in `i` is my choice of English figure); the -čuγ̇u is the past -žuγ̇u after r. Nilqa is not explained by the Ming, which says 人名 'a person's name'; I keep it as part of the name.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Wang Qan, a ruler's name [人名]
Nilqa-Senggum, a man's name (the element Nilqa is not explained) [人名]
to be left behind [落後了有來]

sentences.t: Tein dura qočoruγsan-i Žamuqa uqažu
sentences.l: Thus heart left-behind-one-(object), Žamuqa perceiving,
sentences.i: Jamuqa, perceiving that Chinggis's heart had thus cooled,
sentences.n: Tein dura qočoruγsan-i: qočoruγsan-i is qočor- + the past participle -uγsan, 'what was left behind', + the accusative -i (Ming 後了的 行), so dura qočoruγsan-i is 'the heart's having been left behind', the object of uqažu. Whether the participle really governs dura, or names the man (the heart-cooled one), the grammar cannot settle; the English follows the Ming's sense. uqažu, 'perceiving' (覺着), is another converb; Jamuqa is its subject.

morph.gloss: to be left behind [後了的 行]

sentences.t: γaqai žil qabur Žamuqa, Altan, Qučar, Qardakidai, Ebügežin, Nobukin, Sügeġetei, Toγ̇oril Qačiγ̇un-Beki tede bolun nigen ejeten bolžu
sentences.l: Pig year spring, Žamuqa, Altan, Qučar, Qardakidai, Ebügežin, Nobukin, Sügeġetei, Toγ̇oril, Qačiγ̇un-Beki, they becoming, one counsel-having becoming,
sentences.i: In the spring of the Pig year, Jamuqa, Altan, Quchar, the Qardakidai, the Ebügejin, the Nobukin, Sügegetei, To'oril and Qachi'un-Beki, becoming of one mind in counsel,
sentences.n: The list stays whole. γaqai žil qabur is 'pig year, spring', Ming 猪兒 年 春. Altan and Qučar are given just as personal names by the Ming (人名). Qardakidai, Ebügežin, Nobukin are glossed 種人, 'a kind of people', so clan or people names rather than persons; the English follows with 'the …'. tede bolun nigen ejeten bolžu: tede 'they', bolun 'being' (a converb, Ming 做), nigen 'one', ejeten, Ming 商議, 'counsel-having'. I split ejeten as eje 'counsel' + -ten possessive 'having' (the -tü/-tai type, here in the plural form), but this is a reading rather than a solid analysis. bolžu is bol- + -žu: 'becoming one of counsel', a converb chain with two 'becoming's; I read it as 'agreeing together'. Shiratori prints no comma between Toγ̇oril and Qačiγ̇un-Beki; the Ming glosses each 人名 separately and each speaks alone below, so I read two men. This Toγ̇oril has no title (Ming 人名 only), though the spelling is that of Qan To'oril of the Kereid; I do not decide whether they are one man. The chain runs on into the next unit.

morph.gloss: Qardakidai, a people or clan name [種人]
Ebügejin, a people or clan name [種人]
Nobukin, a people or clan name [種人]

sentences.t: neġüžü odču Žežeġer Ündür-ün gerü-de Ber-Keġeled-te Nilqa-Seṅgüm-dür odču
sentences.l: Camp-moving, going, Žežeġer Ündür-of shade-at, Ber-Keġeled-at, Nilqa-Seṅgüm-to going,
sentences.i: moved camp, and went to the shaded side of Jeje'er Ündür, at Ber-Ke'eled, and went to Nilqa-Senggum,
sentences.n: Two place-expressions with dative-locative endings (gerü-de, Ber-Keġeled-te), the genitive Ündür-ün, and a person with -dür; the Ming gives Žežeġer 地名 'a place', Ündür-ün 山名的 'of the mountain' (not 'of the high', although ündür means 'high'; I take it as a mountain-name), gerü-de 陰行 'on the shade/north side', Ber-Keġeled-te 地名(行). The translation 'shaded side of Jeje'er Ündür' is my reading; the Ming does not say whether the camp lay on the north slope. neġüžü is 'moving camp' (起着) and odču is od- 'go' + -ču (Ming 去着, 'going'); both -ču and -žu are the same converb, the consonant changing with the stem. The chain still runs: the next unit is the speech that comes at the end of it.

morph.gloss: back, the back or shaded side (Ming 陰 'shade'; compare gerü-deče 'from behind') [陰行]
Nilqa-Senggum, a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.t: Žamuqa ülgin ügülerün:
sentences.l: Žamuqa praise speaking:
sentences.i: Jamuqa spoke a praise (or figure of speech):
sentences.n: ülgin: Ming 讚, 'praise'. It stands for what is to come and means, I think, a set speech or figurative saying (the later word ülgür means a parable, but I will not lean on that); Jamuqa is about to slander Temüjin by indirection, which fits a figure better than praise. The reading is uncertain. ügülerün is the converb of speech, 'saying'; it opens the quotation.

sentences.t: Temüžin anda min-u Naiman-u Tajaṅ Qān-dur keletü elčitü bijü.
sentences.l: "Temüžin, sworn-brother mine, Naiman's Tajaṅ Qān-to, speech-having, envoy-having is.
sentences.i: "Temüjin, my sworn brother, has words and has envoys to Tayang Qan of the Naiman.
sentences.n: anda 'sworn brother' is the word of §164's pact (Ming 契交); min-u 'my' is the genitive of bi (min- + -u); it stands after anda, 'sworn brother mine', as in §§158–164. keletü and elčitü are the possessive -tü of 'having': kele 'tongue, speech' + -tü, 'tongue-having' (話有的), elči 'envoy' + -tü, 'envoy-having' (使臣有的). This is the pattern -tü/-tu/-tai/-tei = 'having, with', and the Ming's 有的 is its signal. Together with Qān-dur (dative-locative, 'to the Qan') it says he is in communication, by word and envoy, with Tayang of the Naiman. bijü is the present 'is' (Ming 有) and carries both. bijü is a written verb, so `l` has 'is'; nothing further is supplied. Tajaṅ is Shiratori's spelling for the Naiman ruler.

morph.gloss: Qan, sovereign (short form of qaγan) [(皇帝)行]

sentences.t: Aman in-ü ečige köġü keġežü amu.
sentences.l: Mouth his, father son saying is.
sentences.i: His mouth says 'father and son.'
sentences.n: aman in-ü is 'mouth his' (the third-person genitive in-ü set after its noun, as an-u after back vowels). ečige köġü is 'father, son', and keġežü amu is 'saying is': keġe- 'say' + -žü, a- 'be' + the present -mu. The sense 'only his mouth says it' comes from the contrast with the following line, not from any ending; 'father son' is bare, with no case, and I take it as an allusion to the father-and-son pact of §164 between Temüjin and Wang Qan. That is my reading of the allusion; the grammar gives only the words.

sentences.t: Abüri in-ü öġere bijü.
sentences.l: Nature his other is.
sentences.i: His nature is otherwise.
sentences.n: abüri 'nature, disposition' is Ming 德性; öġere is glossed 𠮠 here (a rare character that may show as a box; the house entry reads 𠮠 'apart, separately'), which I take as 'different, otherwise'. bijü 'is'. A short, plain clause; the contrast is with the mouth of the line before.

sentences.t: Itegežüġü amui ta.
sentences.l: Relying are you.
sentences.i: You are trusting him.
sentences.n: itegežüġü is itege- 'to trust, rely on' (Ming 倚仗着) with the ending -žüġü, which has the shape of the past -žuγ̇u/-žüġüi of keġežüġüi elsewhere in this part; the Ming's 着 reads it as a converb, and a converb before amui 'is' is odd, so I take the pair as 'are trusting'. Uncertain. The object, Temüjin, is not named. ta is the plural-polite 'you' (Ming 您); Jamuqa speaks to Nilqa-Seṅgüm, to whom the company has just gone (the plural-polite ta may take in his father).

morph.gloss: ending -žüġü (the shape of the past -žuγ̇u, but the Ming 着 reads a converb; uncertain)

sentences.t: Ese nemdeġešü tan-a jaγ̇u bolqu.
sentences.l: Not-yet forestalling-if, you-to what will-be?
sentences.i: If you have not got in first, what will become of you?
sentences.n: ese before a conditional: ese nemdeġešü, Ming 不曾 攙先呵, 'if you have not got in first, cut in before him'. The stem nemde- is inferred from the Ming 攙先, and the conditional is -ġešü, Shiratori's spelling with š of -ġesü (呵), as in nögčiġešü. tan-a is the stem tan- 'you' (before case endings) with the dative-locative -a, Ming 您行 'to you'. jaγ̇u bolqu: 'what will become', participle in -qu. Note that Jamuqa's 'not-yet' (ese) is the negative we expect with a past or completed action, so 'if you have not yet …', not 'if you do not'.

morph.gloss: to forestall, cut in first (stem inferred from the Ming 攙先) [攙先呵]
conditional: if (printed with š, as in nögčiġešü)
you (plural, polite; stem before case endings) [您行]

sentences.t: Temüžin anda-dur morilaγ̇asu bi kündelen-eče oroldusu" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Temüžin sworn-brother-to, if-mounting, I from-the-flank join-let-me," said.
sentences.i: If you ride against the sworn brother Temüjin, I will join you from the flank," he said.
sentences.n: anda-dur is 'to the sworn brother' (Ming 契交行), which with morilaγ̇asu gives 'against', and morilaγ̇asu is mori(n) 'horse' + -la- 'to mount' + conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 上馬呵, 'if mounted'): 'if you set out against him'. kündelen-eče is Ming 自橫裏 'from the side, the flank'; the stem is uncertain. oroldusu: oro- 'enter' + reciprocal -ldu- 'together' + the optative -su (Ming 共入, no 呵, so not a conditional): 'let me enter with you'. The speech is closed by keġežüġüi, past 'said' (-žüġüi is the front-vowel form of -žuγ̇ui). 'I join' is a promise to join the attack on Temüjin.

morph.gloss: sworn brother, pledged friend [契交 行]
sideways, from the flank (Ming 橫裏; stem uncertain) [自橫裏]

sentences.t: Altan, Qučar qojar ügülerün: Ba Höġelün eke-jin köġün-i aqa-ji alažu deġü-ji tebčižü ögsügei" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Altan, Qučar, the-two, speaking: "We, Höġelün mother-of son-(object), elder-brother-(object) killing, younger-brother-(object) casting-aside, let-us-give," said.
sentences.i: Altan and Quchar, the two, said: "We will give up Högelün's son: killing the elder brother and casting off the younger."
sentences.n: The speakers are Altan and Quchar, each introduced by his name only (Ming 人名). ba is 'we, exclusive' (Ming 俺, against the inclusive bida 咱). Höġelün eke-jin köġün-i is 'Högelün the mother's son, object', with genitive -jin after the vowel and the accusative -i; I take Högelün as Temüjin's mother (the Ming says only 母名, 'a mother's name'). aqa-ji and deġü-ji are 'the elder brother' and 'the younger brother' as objects; alažu 'killing' and tebčižü 'casting aside' are two converbs. ögsügei is ög- 'give' + -sügei, Ming 與咱, 'let us give'. What is 'given' and to whom is not stated, and the middle two clauses, 'killing the elder, casting off the younger', are cryptic: they may describe what is to be done to the family around Temüjin, or what Altan and Quchar are ready to do to their own kin. This is a first reading, not an understanding.

morph.gloss: Högelün, a woman's name (the mother of Temüjin) [母名]

sentences.t: Ebügežin, Nojakin, Qartaγ̇ad, ügülerün: "Γar in-ü γardažu köl in-ü köldežü ögsügei" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Ebügežin, Nojakin, Qartaγ̇ad, speaking: "Hand his laying-hand-on, foot his seizing, let-us-give," said.
sentences.i: The Ebügejin, the Nojakin and the Qarta'ad said: "Seizing him by the hand and by the foot, we will give him up."
sentences.n: Three more peoples (Ming 種人), who speak together. γar 'hand' and köl 'foot' each take a verbal ending: γardažu (Ming 拿着) is γar + -da- + -žu, and köldežü köl + -de- + -žü, 'laying hands on', 'taking by the foot', with the back-vowel and front-vowel forms of the same converb; in-ü 'his' is the third-person genitive. 'Hand his seizing, foot his seizing' is a plain parallelism and the English follows. ögsügei again: 'let us give'. The object ('him') is not named, but 'his' is presumably Temüjin, which fits the previous speech's 'Högelün's son'.

morph.gloss: Ebügejin, a people or clan name [種人]
Nojakin, a people or clan name [種人]
Qarta'ad, a people or clan name [種人]
verb-forming: to lay a hand on
verb-forming: to lay hold by the foot (as γarda- 'lay a hand on')

sentences.t: Toγ̇oril ügülerün: "Araγača odču Temüžin-i ulus in-ü abuja.
sentences.l: Toγ̇oril speaking: "Reckoning, going, Temüžin-(object), people his, take-let-us.
sentences.i: To'oril said: "Reckoning it so, let us go and take Temüjin's people.
sentences.n: araγača is Ming 料來, 'on reckoning, by estimate', a particle or postposition whose force I cannot fix; I render 'Reckoning it so' only to keep the word visible; the force is a guess. Temüžin-i has the accusative; ulus in-ü is 'people his', ulus 'people, realm' (Ming 百姓 'common people' in this section) and in-ü 'his'. abuja is ab- 'take' + hortative -uja, Ming 要咱, 'let us take'; the 咱 is the inclusive 'let us'. So To'oril proposes taking Temüjin's following rather than his person, as the next sentence says.

morph.gloss: as for, going by (form unclear) [料來]
Temüjin, a man's name [(人)名 行]

sentences.t: Ulus-jan abdaγ̇asu ulus ügeiġü boluγ̇asu jakikün tede" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Own people if-taken, people without if-it-becomes, what-will-do they?" said.
sentences.i: If their own people are taken from them, and they are left without people, what will they do?" he said.
sentences.n: A chain of two conditionals: ulus-jan abdaγ̇asu, ulus ügeiġü boluγ̇asu, 'people-own if taken, people without if it becomes'. -jan is the reflexive-possessive after a consonant: 'their own' (the Ming's 自的行 pairs it with 行, though the word is the subject of a passive; I take the Ming's 行 here as an echo, not a case). abdaγ̇asu is ab- 'take' + passive -da- + conditional -γ̇asu, 'if (they) are taken'. ügeiġü 'without, there being none' (無). jakikün is the future-participle question, 'what shall one do?' (Ming 待如何), and tede 'they' (plural of tere) is the doer. The two conditionals in -γ̇asu (back-vowel form) are the 'if … if' of the argument.

sentences.t: Qačiγ̇un-Beki ügülerün: "Nilqa-Seṅgüm köġün čima-ji jaγ̇u sedkiġesü urtu-jin üžüġür-e gün-ü hiraγ̇ur-a kürülčesü" keġežü
sentences.l: Qačiγ̇un-Beki speaking: "Nilqa-Seṅgüm, son, you-(object) what thinking-if, long-of end-at, deep-of bottom-at, may-I-reach-together," saying,
sentences.i: Qachi'un-Beki said: "Nilqa-Senggum, son, if I think anything of you, may I reach with you the end of the long and the bottom of the deep," he said.
sentences.n: A difficult speech; the words are clear, the sense less so. Qačiγ̇un-Beki, a man's name (Ming 人名), addresses Nilqa-Seṅgüm as köġün 'son'; whether that is literal or an address I cannot say. čima-ji is the oblique stem čima- 'you' + accusative -ji, Ming 你行. The Ming gives (如何) in brackets for jaγ̇u, meaning 'what' is supplied, and then sedkiġesü, the front-vowel conditional 'if I think'. urtu-jin üžüġür-e is 'at the end of the long' (urtu 'long', -jin genitive, üžüġür 'end', Ming 梢) and gün-ü hiraγ̇ur-a 'at the bottom of the deep' (gün 'deep', hiraγ̇ur 'bottom', Ming 底): a pair of proverbial limits, which I take as a vow to follow him to the farthest end. kürülčesü, Ming 共到我, is kür- 'reach' with an ending -ülče- 'together' and optative -sü: 'may I reach together'. All this is a first reading. The unit ends with keġežü, a converb, and the sentence goes on in §167.

sentences.t: ede üges ügülegdežü Nilqa-Seṅgüm ečige-dür(i)-jen Waṅ-Qan-dur tedeġer üges Saiqan-Tödeġen(i)-jer ügü- ležü iležüġüi.
sentences.l: These words being-said, Nilqa-Seṅgüm, father-own-to Waṅ-Qan-to, those words Saiqan-Tödeġen-through saying, sent.
sentences.i: Having been told these words, Nilqa-Senggum sent word of them to his own father, Wang Qan, through Saiqan-Tödögen.
sentences.n: A new § begins; the subject is now Nilqa-Seṅgüm: ede üges ügülegdežü, 'these words being-said', is a passive converb (ügüle- 'speak' + passive -gde- + -žü, Ming 被說着, 'having been told'): the words that Qačiγ̇un-Beki and the others spoke. ečige-dür(i)-jen is ečige 'father' + dative-locative -dür + the reflexive-possessive -(i)jen (the (i) is Shiratori's bracketed linking vowel), 'to his own father'. Waṅ-Qan-dur repeats it with the name. tedeġer üges, 'those words', is the quotation reported. Saiqan-Tödeġen(i)-jer is a man's name (人名) with an ending -(i)jer of uncertain force: the Ming 敎 'cause, have' makes it 'having Saiqan-Tödeġen say', but the shape is that of an instrumental ('through'). ügü- + ležü is ügüle-žü split across the line. iležüġüi is ile- 'send' + past, Ming 去了 'went'; I read 'sent' because the Ming's 敎去 elsewhere means 'caused to go', but 'went' is possible.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, a ruler's name [人名 行]
Saiqan-Tödögen, a man's name [人名 敎]
ending of uncertain force (the Ming 敎 reads 'caused to …')
to speak (first half of a word split at the line end) [說]

sentences.t: Edeġer üges ügülegdežü Waṅ-Qān ügülerün:
sentences.l: These words being-said, Waṅ-Qān speaking:
sentences.i: Having been told these words, Wang Qan said:
sentences.n: edeġer is 'these' (plural, Ming 這(的)每), the plural of ede. The same passive converb as in the previous unit; the sentence repeats its first half so that the subject can switch to Wang Qan. Nothing new.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, a ruler's name [人名]

sentences.t: "Köġün-i min-u Temüžin-dür jakin tein sedkin bijü.
sentences.l: "Son-(object) my, Temüžin-to why so thinking is?
sentences.i: "Why do you think so of my son Temüjin?
sentences.n: Köġün-i min-u Temüžin-dür is 'son-obj my Temüjin-to': Temüjin, 'my son', is the one thought ill of. The first word carries the accusative -i (Ming 子行) where the dative would be expected beside Temüžin-dür (the Ming's 行 can mark either); I take the two as one phrase, 'to my son Temüjin'. jakin 'why' (Ming 爲甚), tein 'so' (那般), sedkin is sedki- 'think' + -n, bijü 'is': 'why is [one] thinking so?', that is, 'why do you think so of him?'. The subject 'you' is not written; I take it from what follows.

sentences.t: Ta ežiġe tuluγ ima-γ̇ar-i bolžu böġed edöġe köġün-dür min-u tein maγ̇ui sedkiġesü teṅgeri-de ülü taγ̇alaγdaqun bida.
sentences.l: You, until-now, reliance, on-his-account, being, being, now son-to my so bad if-think, Heaven-by not being-loved, we.
sentences.i: You have leaned on him until now; and if you now think so ill of my son, we shall not be loved by Heaven.
sentences.n: The Ming's words are all I have: 到今 倚仗 因他 行 做着 見有 如今: 'until now, relying, on his account, being, being'. ežiġe tuluγ imaγ̇ar-i bolžu böġed is the hardest stretch: I read 'until now you have been leaning on him', but ima-γ̇ar-i (Ming 因他行) I cannot analyse, and tuluγ could also be a postposition 'on account of'. Then edöġe köġün-dür min-u tein maγ̇ui sedkiġesü, 'now if you think so ill of my son', with the front-vowel conditional -ġesü. teṅgeri-de ülü taγ̇alaγdaqun bida is 'by Heaven not loved, we': -de names the agent of a passive (taγ̇ala- 'love' + -γda-), and bida is the inclusive 'we'. ülü here negates a passive participle, 'will not be loved'. I read it as a statement; it may be a rhetorical question, since the repeat a few units on has a question particle.

morph.gloss: until now, up to now [到今]
reliance, support (uncertain; or 'on account of') [倚仗]
on his account, by means of him (form not analysed) [因他 行]
Heaven, the sky as a power [天 行]
not (negates a present or future action, or a converb) [不]

sentences.t: Žamuqa jabudaγ keletü büleġe.
sentences.l: Žamuqa roving speech-having was.
sentences.i: Jamuqa was a man of shifting speech.
sentences.n: jabudaγ keletü: jabu- 'go, wander' (Ming 走作, 'go astray') with a habitual participle -daγ, and keletü, the possessive 'tongue-having': 'one with a roving tongue', that is a double-dealer. büleġe is bü- 'be' + past -leġe, 'was, used to be' (Ming 有來). büleġe is a written verb, so `l` has 'was'.

morph.gloss: to go about, stray (Ming 走作 'go astray') [走作]

sentences.t: Žöb(ü)-ü tab(u)-u ügülen bijü" keġen ese taγ̇alažu iležüġüi.
sentences.l: Right? true? speaking is, saying, not-yet pleased-with, sent.
sentences.i: Is it right? Is it true? — that is how he goes on talking," he said, and, not being won over, he sent [them] off.
sentences.n: Žöb(ü)-ü tab(u)-u: two questions, each a word with the question particle -ü/-u (Ming 是麽 twice, 麽 being a question mark). žöb is 'right, proper'; tab(u) is paired with it and glossed the same by the Ming, so I give 'true'. ügülen bijü is 'speaking is', the converb + 'is'. The sense I take is 'he keeps asking is it right, is it true', that is, he shifts about; the Ming gives no more. keġen closes the quotation. ese taγ̇alažu is 'not-yet being pleased' (Ming 不曾 愛着): ese + converb, a rare use, since ülü is the usual negative before converbs; the Ming 愛 means 'like, be fond of', and I translate it 'was not won over'. iležüġüi (去了) is again 'sent'; the object is understood: Wang Qan sent off the messenger with this answer. First reading.

morph.gloss: so, true (uncertain; pairs with žöb) [是麽]
to love, be pleased with [愛着]

sentences.t: Basa Seṅgüm ügüležü ilerün: "Amatu keletü küġün ügülen böġetele jakin ülü büširegdekü"
sentences.l: Again Seṅgüm speaking, sending: "Mouth-having, tongue-having man speaking while-being, why not to-be-believed?"
sentences.i: Senggum again sent a message: "While a man has a mouth and a tongue and is speaking, why is it not to be believed?"
sentences.n: basa 'again' (Ming 再) and ilerün, ile- 'send' with the time-converb -rün (the Ming's 去 'go' is an alternative: 'going'). amatu keletü küġün is 'mouth-having, tongue-having man' — two -tu/-tü possessives, back and front vowels, Ming 口 有的 舌 有的 (note ama- for aman before a suffix). ügülen böġetele: ügüle- + -n, bü-/böġe- 'be' + -tele, 'while', Ming 有間. büširegdekü is büšire- 'believe' + passive -gde- + participle -kü: 'to be believed, credible' (可信). The sense is Senggum defending Jamuqa's report: a man who can speak should be believed. The quotation continues in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Senggum, son of Wang Qan (personal name) [人名]
to be (böġe- before an ending) [有間]
not (negates a present or future action, or a converb) [不]

sentences.t: keġen žiči-quči ügüležü ileġed jadažu öġesün bejegedün odču ügülerün:
sentences.l: Saying, back-and-forth speaking, sending, being-unable, own-self in-person going, speaking:
sentences.i: So he said, and sent word back and forth; and, having sent and failing, he went himself in person and said:
sentences.n: žiči-quči is a pair (Ming 反復 'back and forth'), the žiči of 'but' with a rhyming second half, and I take it as 'again and again'. ileġed is ile- + the converb -ġed, front-vowel form (Ming 去了). jadažu is jada- 'be in want, be unable' + -žu (Ming 不能着). öġesün 'oneself' (自己) and bejegedün (親身), 'in person': beje 'body' + an ending whose force I cannot give; the Ming's 親身 is what I follow. The chain closes with odču ügülerün, 'going, saying', and opens a new speech.

morph.gloss: back and forth, repeatedly (a reduplicating pair; uncertain) [反復]

sentences.t: "Bel čima-ji edüi büküi čaγ-tur bidan-i jaγ̇un-a ber ülü bolγan bijü.
sentences.l: "Moreover, you-(object) this-much existing time-at, us anything even not making is.
sentences.i: "And in these present times you are not making us anything at all.
sentences.n: A hard sentence whose general sense is clear. bel is Ming 且, 'and, moreover'; čima-ji 'you' (accusative on the oblique stem, 你行); edüi 'so much' (這些), büküi the participle of bü- 'be' (有的), čaγ-tur 'at the time' (時 行). bidan-i is 'us (object)', jaγ̇un-a ber 'to anything even' (甚麽行 也), ülü bolγan 'not making': bol- + causative -γa- + -n, 'making [something] of'. The Ming is plain: 'you, in this time, you do not make us anything'. I read it as Senggum charging Wang Qan with giving his own people no standing; the double accusative (čima-ji … bidan-i) is awkward, and čima-ji may mean 'as for you'.

morph.gloss: so much, just this much [這些]
not (negates a present or future action, or a converb) [不]

sentences.t: Ünen ber Qān ečige-jen čima-ji čaγaγ̇an-a sačaγ̇asu qara-da qaγaγ̇asu
sentences.l: Truly even Qān father-own you-(object), white-at if-snatched, black-at if-choked,
sentences.i: Truly, Qan, my father: if one snatches at you in the white and chokes in the black,
sentences.n: The proverb-like pair: čaγaγ̇an-a sačaγ̇asu 'at the white, if one snatches' (Ming 白行 搶着呵) and qara-da qaγaγ̇asu 'at the black, if one chokes' (黑行 噎着呵). The two conditionals are -γ̇asu again. I take 'white' and 'black' as opposites (good and bad, or fair and foul) and the whole as 'whatever befalls you'; this is a guess, and the Ming gives no help beyond the words. ünen ber is Ming 眞誠 也, 'truly even'; ünen means 'truth' here, not 'ermine' (which the house glossary also has). ečige-jen is the reflexive-possessive -jen on ečige 'father': 'his own father', so Senggum names Wang Qan as 'Qan father' in his own voice, with čima-ji 'you' as the object of the two conditional verbs, whose subject is not written. The Ming gives 搶着 and 噎着 without 被, so I take the verbs as active, not passive; the proverb I do not understand.

morph.gloss: Qan, sovereign (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.t: Qurčaqus-Buiruγ Qān ečige-jin čin-u žoban edüi qurijažu aγsan ulus-i čin-u man-a-u medeġülkü.
sentences.l: Qurčaqus-Buiruγ Qān father-of, your toil, this-much gathering, dwelling people-(object), yours, us-to? shall-be-made-to-know.
sentences.i: Your father Qurchaqus-Buiruq Qan's toil, so much, gathering and settling the people, your people: will they be entrusted to us to manage?
sentences.n: A first reading. Qurčaqus-Buiruγ Qān ečige-jin is 'Qurchaqus-Buiruq Qan, father's' with the genitive -jin; čin-u žoban is 'your toil' (the genitive -u on the stem čin-, žoban 'toil, hardship', Ming 生受). edüi qurijažu aγsan ulus-i, Ming 這些 收拾着 住來的 百姓 行, is 'the people that (he) gathered up and lived', qurija- 'gather' + -žu, a- 'be' + -γsan past participle. The sentence ends man-a-u medeġülkü: man-a 'to us' (exclusive stem man- + -a, Ming 俺行) + -u (the Ming 呵, which may mark a question or just 'as for us'; uncertain) and medeġülkü, mede- 'know' + causative -ġül- + -kü, Ming 敎管麽, 'shall one have us manage?' The question seems to be: will the people be left to us to govern? The parsing of ečige-jin čin-u žoban is open ('your father's toil', as `i` has it, or 'the father's — your — toil'); `l` keeps the words apart. medeġülkü is glossed 敎管, 'teach and manage', so whether the people are handed to us or taught by us is not settled. I do not understand how the white and black proverb joins this; each stands as I read it.

morph.gloss: Qurchaqus-Buiruq, a man's name (one two-part name) [人名]
Qan, sovereign (short form of qaγan) [皇帝]
so much, just this much [這些]
to gather up, collect (stem inferred) [收拾着]
we (exclusive; stem before case endings) [俺行呵]
particle -u (Ming 呵; question or 'as for', uncertain)

sentences.t: Ken-e ber jakin medeġülkü" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Whom-to even, how shall-be-made-to-know?" said.
sentences.i: To anyone at all, how could they be entrusted?" he said.
sentences.n: ken-e ber is 'to whom even' (Ming 任誰 行也, 'to whomsoever'), ken 'who' + dative-locative -e. jakin medeġülkü repeats the verb of the previous line: 'how shall one have [anyone] manage?'. I take it as a rhetorical question: if not to us, to whom? The speaker is Senggum, pressing his father; I do not know what he is asking to be given. First reading, as the previous unit.

sentences.t: Tere üge-dür Waṅ-Qān ügülerün: "Čaγa-γ̇an köġü-ben ker tebčikü.
sentences.l: That word-in, Waṅ-Qān speaking: "Child-own, son-own, how cast-off?
sentences.i: At that, Wang Qan said: "My own child, my own son — how can I cast him off?
sentences.n: tere üge-dür again opens a reply. The doubled reflexive-possessive čaγa-γ̇an köġü-ben, 'own child, own son' (Ming 孩兒 自的行, 兒子 自的行), both end in a vowel (čaγa, köġü) yet one takes -γ̇an and the other -ben, which I do not try to explain (compare dotora-γ̇an, aduγ̇u-ban). The two nouns are the same person, Senggum. ker tebčikü is 'how cast off?' (怎生 棄捨的), ker 'how' with the participle in -kü, a rhetorical question. čaγa 'child' is Ming 孩兒; its form and meaning are not otherwise clear to me.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, a ruler's name [人名]
child (Ming 孩兒) [孩兒 自的(行)]

sentences.t: Ežiġe tuluγ ima-γ̇ar-i bolžu maγ̇ui sedkiġesü žokiqu-ju. Teṅgeri-de ülü taγ̇alaγdaqun bida" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Until-now reliance on-his-account being, bad if-think, fitting-is-it? Heaven-by not being-loved, we," said.
sentences.i: If you have leaned on him until now and think ill of him, is that right? We shall not be loved by Heaven," he said.
sentences.n: Almost a repeat of the speech earlier in this § (ežiġe tuluγ ima-γ̇ar-i bolžu maγ̇ui sedkiġesü, 'until now relying on him, if one thinks ill'), now with the added žokiqu-ju: Ming 且麽有, 'is it so?, is it fitting?'. I read žoki- 'be fitting' + participle -qu + question -ju; the stem is inferred, and the Ming's 且 has no clear counterpart. teṅgeri-de ülü taγ̇alaγdaqun bida appears again, as at the end of the previous speech: 'by Heaven, not loved, we'. I read it as a statement of fear. keġežüġüi closes the quotation. Most of this repeats the earlier notes; the repeated hard words keep the same doubts.

morph.gloss: until now, up to now [到今]
reliance, support (uncertain; or 'on account of') [倚仗]
on his account, by means of him (form not analysed) [他 行]
Heaven, the sky as a power [天 行]
not (negates a present or future action, or a converb) [不]

sentences.t: Tere üge-dür köġün in-ü Nilqa-Seṅgüm maγ̇uilažu egüden oγ̇orču γ̇arčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: That word-in, son his Nilqa-Seṅgüm, being-vexed, door going(?), went-out.
sentences.i: At that his son Nilqa-Senggum, vexed, made for the door and went out.
sentences.n: The converb chain with its unmarked subject: maγ̇uilažu is maγ̇ui 'bad' + -la- 'to be, to feel' + -žu, Ming 煩惱着, 'being vexed'; oγ̇orču is oγ̇or- + -ču (the Ming here gives 去着 'going'; the house entry reads the stem 'throw' from an earlier passage with 丢; the stem is uncertain); and γ̇arčuγ̇u is γ̇ar- 'go out' + the past -čuγ̇u (that is, -žuγ̇u after r), Ming 出去了. The object of oγ̇orču is egüden 'door' (門). The Ming says only that he went (去着) by the door (門); `i` keeps to that.

morph.gloss: to go, make for (stem uncertain; house entry 'throw', Ming here 去着) [去着]

sentences.t: Žiči köġün-ü-ġen Seṅgüm-ün duran qairalažu urižu ireġülžü Waṅ-Qān ügülerün:
sentences.l: But son-own-of Seṅgüm-of heart cherishing, calling, causing-to-come, Waṅ-Qān speaking:
sentences.i: But Wang Qan, holding dear the heart of his own son Senggum, called him back and said:
sentences.n: The subject comes last, as often: Waṅ-Qān is the doer of all the converbs before it (qairalažu, urižu, ireġülžü). köġün-ü-ġen is köġün 'son' + genitive -ü + the reflexive-possessive -ġen, 'of his own son', Ming 子 自的行; Seṅgüm-ün is Ming 人名的; duran is 'heart' (dura) with a final -n I cannot explain (a reflexive ending?). qairalažu, Ming 愛惜着, 'holding dear, cherishing'. ireġülžü is ire- 'come' + causative -ġül- + -žü, 'making come', so 'summoning' (敎來着).

morph.gloss: Senggum, son of Wang Qan (personal name) [人名的]
to hold dear, cherish (Ming 愛惜) [愛惜着]
Wang Qan, a ruler's name [人名]

sentences.t: "Teṅgeri-de maqa taγ̇alaγdaqun-u bida.
sentences.l: "Heaven-by perhaps-not being-loved? we.
sentences.i: "Are we perhaps not loved by Heaven?
sentences.n: maqa is Ming 莫 here (the house entry has 知他 'who knows' from another passage), a particle read as 'perhaps not'; the question particle -u on taγ̇alaγdaqun-u (Ming 被愛麽) makes the question explicit, which the earlier two occurrences lacked. teṅgeri-de (agent of the passive) and bida 'we' (inclusive) are as before. The sense I give, 'perhaps not loved', rests on the Ming's 莫 'perhaps not' and is uncertain.

morph.gloss: Heaven, the sky as a power [天 行]
perhaps (not) (Ming here 莫; house entry 知他 'who knows') [莫]

sentences.t: Köġün-i ker tebčišü keġemüi.
sentences.l: Son-(object) how cast-off-would? says.
sentences.i: How would I cast off a son? I say.
sentences.n: köġün-i with its accusative, ker 'how', tebčišü, tebči- + -šü (Shiratori's spelling of -sü; the Ming 要 says 'would'), and keġemüi, keġe- 'say' + the present -müi, Ming 說有, 'says'. I take the speaker's 'says' as 'I say'; it may be 'one says', a proverb.

morph.gloss: optative: would (a spelling of -sü; Ming 要; uncertain)

sentences.t: Ta čidan ele üiledüdkün ta mededkün" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: You able only, do; you know," said.
sentences.i: Do what you are able to do; you know for yourselves," he said.
sentences.n: Wang Qan gives way. čidan is čida- 'be able' + -n; ele (Ming 但) 'only, indeed', with its force not settled. üiledüdkün and mededkün are plural-polite imperatives in -dkün (Ming 做您, 自知者, 'do, and know for yourselves'); a final -n is part of the same ending. üiledüdkün is üile- 'do' with an element -dü- inside; I do not divide it further. ta 'you' is plural-polite, Wang Qan to Senggum. keġežüġüi closes the quotation.

morph.gloss: only, indeed (Ming 但; force uncertain) [但]

sentences.t: Tendēče Seṅgüm ügülerün: "Müd-lü bidan-u Čaγ̇ur-Beki-ji γuju büleġe.
sentences.l: From-there Seṅgüm speaking: "They-but our Čaγ̇ur-Beki-(object) asking was.
sentences.i: After that Senggum said: "They, however, had asked for our Cha'ur-Beki.
sentences.n: The § begins with tendēče, tende 'there' + ablative -ēče in the long-vowel spelling (Ming 自那裏). müd-lü is Ming 他每但 'they but': müd 'they' and -lü 'but, however' (my gloss of the Ming 但; uncertain). The sense: the Chinggis side had asked for Cha'ur-Beki, and Senggum is now laying a trap that depends on that. γuju is the converb of 'ask for' (索); büleġe 'was, used to be'. Note bidan-u, 'our', for Senggum's own sister.

morph.gloss: Senggum, son of Wang Qan (personal name) [人名]
Cha'ur-Beki, a woman's name [女名 行]
to ask for, claim (stem uncertain; the converb) [索]

sentences.t: Edöġe buγ̇ulžar idere iredkün keġen
sentences.l: Now betrothal-feast to-eat come, saying,
sentences.i: Now, saying 'Come and eat the betrothal feast,'
sentences.n: edöġe 'now', buγ̇ulžar, Ming 許婚筵席, 'betrothal feast'; idere is ide- 'eat' + a purpose converb -re, Ming 喫, and iredkün is ire- 'come' + plural-polite imperative -dkün (Ming 來您), as in the last §. keġen closes the quotation again. The speech this belongs to is a plan: to summon Chinggis on this pretext.

sentences.t: üdür bolžažü urižu ireġülžü tende barija" keġel- dužu "Že" keġen eje baraldužu"
sentences.l: Day appointing, calling, causing-to-come, there let-us-seize," saying-together, "So be it," saying, counsel agreeing,"
sentences.i: fixing a day, calling him and making him come, let us seize him there." Saying this together, and saying "So be it," they settled the plan.
sentences.n: The chain of converbs: bolžažü (約會着, 'agreeing a meeting': bolža- 'fix, appoint' is a guess from the Ming), urižu 'calling', ireġülžü 'causing to come' — and then tende barija, Ming 那裏 拿咱 (the 咱 'let us'), 'let us seize [him] there'. barija is bari- 'seize' + -ja, like the hortative -je; the Ming here has 拿咱, with 咱 'let us' (the house entry, from a passage glossed 拿住, has none), so `i` has 'let us seize'. keġel- + dužu is one word split at the line end: keġeldužu, keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldu- + -žu, 'saying to one another' (共說着). že is the particle of assent (那般者), and eje baraldužu is 'counsel having settled' (商議 定着): baraldu- 'settle together' is inferred. Shiratori's quotation mark closes after barija, so I take everything up to there (Edöġe … barija) as part of Senggum's speech, a plan in the converb chain, not events; keġeldužu … baraldužu is then the narrator's, the party agreeing. The marks do not nest cleanly in the printed text.

morph.gloss: to fix, appoint (Ming 約會; stem uncertain) [約會着]
ending of a call: let us (uncertain)
so be it, very well (particle) [那般者︀]
to settle together, agree (stem inferred) [定着]

sentences.t: Čaγ̇ur-Beki-ji ögüje buγ̇ulžar idere iredkün keġen ilebe.
sentences.l: Čaγ̇ur-Beki-(object) let-us-give, betrothal-feast to-eat come, saying, sent.
sentences.i: "Let us give Cha'ur-Beki; come and eat the betrothal feast," they said, and sent.
sentences.n: The message itself: ögüje is ög- 'give' + hortative -üje, Ming 與咱 'let us give'; the rest as in the previous units. ilebe is ile- 'send' + -be (Ming 去了). The invitation seems to be a lie, since the plan was to seize the guest; the text leaves this to the reader.

morph.gloss: Cha'ur-Beki, a woman's name [女名 行]

sentences.t: Uriγdažu Čiṅgis Qaγan harban haran aisurun žaγ̇ura Müṅlig ečige-jin ger-tür qonoγ̇asu tende Müṅlig ečige ügülerün:
sentences.l: Being-summoned, Čiṅgis Qaγan, ten people coming, midway, Müṅlig father-of home-at, if-stayed-the-night, there Müṅlig father speaking:
sentences.i: Summoned, Chinggis Qahan, coming with ten men, on the way stayed the night at the home of Father Münlig. There Father Münlig said:
sentences.n: uriγdažu is uri- 'call' + passive -γda- + -žu, Ming 被喚着 'being called'. harban haran, 'ten people' (十 人); aisurun, aisu- 'come' + -run (來時); žaγ̇ura is žaγ̇ur 'middle' + -a (路間), 'on the road'. Müṅlig ečige-jin ger-tür, Ming 人名 父的 家 裏, 'at Münlig father's house'; I treat ečige 'father' as a title or style of address here (the Ming has simply 父), 'Father Münlig'. qonoγ̇asu is qono- 'stay the night' + conditional -γ̇asu, Ming 宿呵: the conditional is used for the time of staying, 'when he stayed'. The long converb chain ends with ügülerün and a colon.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Čaγ̇ur-Beki-ji γuγ̇asu müd-lü bidan-i doramžilažu ülü ögün büleġe;
sentences.l: "Čaγ̇ur-Beki-(object) if-asked, they-but us looking-down-on, not giving, was;
sentences.i: "When we asked for Cha'ur-Beki, they looked down on us and would not give her;
sentences.n: γuγ̇asu is the third spelling of the 'ask for' stem (Ming 索阿, where 阿 looks like a slip for the conditional marker 呵; the house entry reads the ending as uncertain) with the conditional sense 'when asked'. müd-lü 'they but' as before; bidan-i 'us (object)'; doramžilažu 'looking down on' (下覻着), with ülü ögün büleġe, 'not giving was'. The speaker is Münlig, who is on Chinggis's side. The semicolon is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: Cha'ur-Beki, a woman's name [女名 行]
to look down on, slight [下覻着]
not (negates a present or future action, or a converb) [不]

sentences.t: edöġe ker buruγ̇uj-a buγ̇ulžar idere urižuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Now how specially betrothal-feast to-eat calling-have?
sentences.i: now why have they specially called us to eat a betrothal feast?
sentences.n: edöġe, ker 'how, why', buruγ̇uj-a 'specially' (特地, form uncertain), buγ̇ulžar idere 'to eat the betrothal feast', and urižuγ̇u, uri- 'call' + past -žuγ̇u. The Ming glosses idere 喫來 and urižuγ̇u 喫着, 'eating'; the second looks like a slip for 喚着 'calling', since the stem uri- means 'call' everywhere else. I follow the stem, not the gloss. The translation 'have called' is therefore my choice.

sentences.t: Öġed(i)-jen jekežilekün haran buruγ̇uj-a jakin ögsü keġen uriqun büleġei.
sentences.l: Selves great-making people specially, why give, saying, calling were.
sentences.i: Why were such self-important people specially calling us, saying 'I will give'?
sentences.n: öġed(i)-jen is öġed 'selves' (Ming 自每) with the reflexive-possessive -(i)jen; jekežilekün haran is 'great-making people' (做大的 人), with jekežile-, as in Senggum's jekežilen above; haran 'people' (Ming 人). buruγ̇uj-a jakin ögsü keġen uriqun büleġei is 'specially why give, saying, calling they were': ögsü is ög- 'give' + optative -sü, and uriqun is uri- + a participle -qun (Ming 喚). The reading is a first one: the sense appears to be 'why do those who give themselves airs now offer her?'. büleġei is the past, a variant of büleġe.

morph.gloss: optative: let it be given, I will give

sentences.t: Žöb(ü)-ü tab(u)-u sedkil bi.
sentences.l: Right? true? heart there-is.
sentences.i: Is it right? Is it true? I have a doubt.
sentences.n: Žöb(ü)-ü tab(u)-u again, the paired questions with their particle -ü/-u (是麽, as in §167). sedkil 'heart, mind' (心) and bi, Ming 有, 'is'. The Ming gives no 'doubt'; that is the sense I draw from the two questions put to one's own mind. Münlig begins to counsel Chinggis.

morph.gloss: so, true (uncertain; pairs with žöb) [是麽]

sentences.t: Köġün uqažu oldaqu.
sentences.l: Son perceiving, may-go.
sentences.i: Son, being aware, one may go.
sentences.n: Köġün 'son' addresses Chinggis. uqažu 'perceiving, being aware' (省着), oldaqu, Ming 可去 'may go': I cannot identify the stem. The reading as 'you may go' sits oddly with the advice that follows, which is to decline the feast, so this may be a different sense; first reading, not understood.

morph.gloss: may go, should go (stem not identified) [可去]

sentences.t: Qabur bolba.
sentences.l: Spring became.
sentences.i: Spring has come.
sentences.n: qabur 'spring' (春), bolba, bol- + past -ba, 'became'. A plain pair, the start of Münlig's excuse.

sentences.t: Aduγ̇un bidan-u turuγad bi.
sentences.l: Herd our lean is.
sentences.i: Our horses are lean.
sentences.n: aduγ̇un 'herd of horses' (馬羣); turuγad, turuγ 'lean' + plural -ad (痩每); bi, 'is'. The state of the herds in spring, the thin season.

sentences.t: Aduγ̇u-ban težiġeje keġen šiltažu ileje"
sentences.l: Herd-own let-us-fatten, saying, excusing, let-us-send."
sentences.i: Saying 'Let us fatten our own herd' as an excuse, let us send [them]."
sentences.n: aduγ̇u-ban is aduγ̇u(n) 'herd' + the reflexive-possessive -ban, 'our (one's) own herd' (馬羣 自的行); težiġeje is težiġe- 'fatten, rear' + the hortative -je, Ming 養咱. šiltažu, Ming 推辭着, 'making an excuse'; ileje, ile- + -je, Ming 敎去咱, 'let us send (word)'. The quotation ends. Münlig's plan: send an excuse rather than the man himself.

morph.gloss: herd of horses [馬羣 自的行]
to make an excuse, decline (Ming 推辭) [推辭着]

sentences.t: keġežü ülü odun Buqatai, Kiratai qojar-i "buγ̇ulžar idedkün" keġežü iležü.
sentences.l: Saying, not going, Buqatai, Kiratai, the-two-(object) "betrothal-feast eat-you," saying, sending.
sentences.i: So saying, he did not go; he sent Buqatai and Kiratai, the two, saying "Eat the betrothal feast."
sentences.n: keġežü ülü odun: ülü before a converb, 'not going' (Ming 不 去); odun is od- + -un. The two men are named only (人名). qojar-i takes the accusative: the two are the objects of iležü (敎去着 'causing to go', here 'sending off'), with the plural-polite imperative idedkün (ide- 'eat' + -dkün, Ming 喫您) as their instruction. The subject, Chinggis, is carried over from before; Münlig's words end at ileje.

morph.gloss: not (negates a present or future action, or a converb) [不]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Müṅlig ečige-jin ger-tēče qariba.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan Müṅlig father-of home-from returned.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan turned back from Father Münlig's home.
sentences.n: ger-tēče is ger 'home' + the ablative -ēče in long-vowel spelling (家 處), qariba is qari- 'turn back' + past -ba (囘了). A plain sentence.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Buqatai, Kiratai qojar-i kürküi-lüġe "seregdebe bida; manaγar erte bučižu barija" keġeldübe.
sentences.l: Buqatai, Kiratai, the-two-(object) arriving-as-soon-as, "was-noticed we; tomorrow early surrounding let-us-seize," said-together.
sentences.i: When Buqatai and Kiratai, the two, arrived: "We have been found out; tomorrow, early, let us surround and seize," they said together.
sentences.n: The end of the part, with the subject not named: the Senggum side, who see that the guest has not come. kürküi-lüġe is kür- 'arrive' + the participle -küi + -lüġe 'with' (Ming 到了呵), 'as soon as arriving' (tentative). seregdebe is Ming 被覺了, 'was perceived', a passive (sere- 'be alert' + -gde- + -be) with bida 'we': 'we have been noticed', that is, our plan is known. manaγar erte (明日 在前) is 'tomorrow, early'; bučižu is buči- 'surround' (Ming 圍着) + -žu; barija 'let us seize' as before; the object is not stated and may be Buqatai and Kiratai (qojar-i is accusative) or Chinggis; I leave it open. keġeldübe is keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldü- + -be, 'they said to each other' (共說了).

morph.gloss: to notice, be alert (stem inferred) [被覺了]
ending of a call: let us (uncertain)
